name: ACENEXT-P
uses: Relief of pain, inflammation, and swelling, including muscle pain, back pain, joint pain, toothache, arthritis, and pain from minor injuries.
dosage: Typically 1 tablet once or twice daily as prescribed by the doctor. Take with food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not exceed the prescribed dose.
side_effects: Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, dizziness, and diarrhoea. Prolonged or excessive use may cause stomach, kidney, or liver problems.

name: BRUFEN 400
uses: Relief of pain, fever, and inflammation, including headache, toothache, body pain, menstrual pain, cold-related pain, and mild arthritis.
dosage: Typically 400 mg up to 3 times daily as directed by a doctor. Take with or after food or milk. Do not exceed the prescribed dose.
side_effects: Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, heartburn, bloating, diarrhoea, and constipation. Long-term or excessive use can cause stomach bleeding or kidney problems.

name: DOLO 650
uses: Relief of fever and mild-to-moderate pain such as headache, toothache, muscle ache, body ache, sore throat, and pain associated with common cold.
dosage: 1 tablet when required, with at least 4 hours between doses. Do not take more than 4 tablets in 24 hours unless specifically directed by a doctor.
side_effects: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses. May occasionally cause nausea or stomach discomfort. Excessive doses can cause serious liver damage.

name: GELUSIL MPS
uses: Relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion, sour stomach, and gas or bloating caused by trapped gas.
dosage: For the liquid formulation, typically 5-10 mL (1-2 teaspoonfuls) after meals or when symptoms occur, as directed. Shake the bottle well before use.
side_effects: May cause constipation, diarrhoea, nausea, or stomach discomfort. Excessive or prolonged use may cause electrolyte disturbances.

name: LEVIPIL 500
uses: An anti-epileptic medicine used to prevent and control seizures (fits) in epilepsy. It may be used alone or with other anti-seizure medicines.
dosage: Dose varies according to the type of seizure and individual response. Take exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food.
side_effects: Sleepiness, dizziness, fatigue, weakness, decreased appetite, irritability, and mood or behavioural changes.

name: LEVOCETIRIZINE 5
uses: Relief of allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, watery or itchy eyes, itching, hives, and other allergic skin reactions.
dosage: Adults and adolescents generally take 5 mg once daily, usually in the evening or as directed by a doctor.
side_effects: Sleepiness, tiredness, dry mouth, headache, and dizziness.

name: LOPERAMIDE 2
uses: Short-term control of diarrhoea by reducing the movement of the intestines.
dosage: For adults, a common regimen is 4 mg initially followed by 2 mg after each loose stool. Do not exceed the recommended daily maximum and use only as directed. Do not use for bloody diarrhoea or dysentery unless specifically advised by a doctor.
side_effects: Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, and abdominal cramps.

name: METROGYL 400
uses: Treatment of infections caused by certain bacteria and parasites, including some infections of the stomach and intestines, skin, reproductive organs, bones, lungs, and other areas.
dosage: The dose and duration vary considerably depending on the infection. A commonly prescribed adult regimen is 400 mg 2-3 times daily, but it should be taken strictly according to the doctor's prescription and the complete course should be finished.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, headache, loss of appetite, and a metallic taste. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for the period advised after the last dose.
